messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Potential sensitive-data exposure detected in 'private-deployments' sync job - rule: s3-creds-in-logs. Severity: P2. Auto-page: oncall rotation.

Ben (oncall): hitting this now. brief summary pls — what triggered?

IncidentBot: Detection details: automated scan found 3 log lines containing 'aws_access_key_id' in last 24h from customer-managed VPC sync task. Task owner: private-sync-service. Sample (redacted) included. No confirmed exfil.

Priya S: I'm on it. First priority: scope. Which customers' sync tasks? Are these our internal infra jobs or customer-owned sidecars?

Alex R (SRE): early look — appears to be a customer-managed private deployment that pulled a Redwood sync helper image. Logs aggregated to our temporary ingestion queue for 18 minutes during a failed rotation. Likely limited to 2 customers (cust-phi-1, cust-pii-2).

Jia (Ops): creating an isolated search on logs: `index=ingest source=private-sync service:private-sync` and limiting to `aws_access_key_id`. Running now. ETA ~8m.

Ben (oncall): paging security & legal: @Mona (Legal) please ack. Tyler (CS) FYI because customers may need notification.

Mona (Legal): acknowledged. Need exact scope before any external communication. Also, check contract/regulatory obligations for both customers (PHI? PII?). If PHI, 72-hour window rules may apply.

Tyler (CS): flagged both accounts; opening support hold so we can reach out as soon as we have confirmation. Don't send any external message until Legal signs off on content.

Priya S: updates from log search: found three files with leaked keys: two from cust-phi-1 (one file contains partial token, likely rotated within 30m) and one from cust-pii-2. Keys appear to be short-lived, probably created during a failed rotation. No evidence of usage in downstream requests in token logs.

Alex R (SRE): check runtime metrics for lateral use: `aws_cloudtrail` hits for those keys — none observed. Also checked egress patterns from those containers — no unusual S3 GET/PUT outside expected cadence.

Jia (Ops): job that sent logs blamed on misconfigured logging level in helper image (DEBUG + full env dump). Fixing image and releasing patch to private-sync-service: `private-sync:2026.03.15-rc1` rolling now.

IncidentBot: Note: handoff scheduled in ~45m per oncall rotation. Current owner: Ben (oncall). Next oncall: Priya S at 1710408200.

Ben (oncall): brief for Priya: scope is 2 customers, no confirmed misuse, exposure via logs during rotation window, mitigation = rotate keys, patch image to stop env dumps, audit cloudtrail. Legal to advise on disclosure threshold.

Mona (Legal): high priority: confirm whether PHI touched S3 objects that were accessible to third parties. If keys were not used, we may be able to provide a scoped notice saying 'potential exposure of credentials' with recommended mitigations. Prepare draft notice for review.

Tyler (CS): suggested customer-facing wording draft (do not send):

"Dear <customer>,
We are contacting you about a potential exposure of short-lived credentials related to your Redwood Private sync task on <date>. We detected these values in temporary logs and have taken steps to contain the issue. At this time we have no evidence that the credentials were used. Actions we recommend: rotate credentials, verify access logs in your cloud account, and confirm with your security team. We will follow up with a full incident report within 72 hours.
Sincerely, Redwood Inference"

Priya S: +1 to customer wording but add concrete mitigations we did (rotated on behalf? or instruct them?). We need to decide whether to rotate keys for them or guide them.

Ben (oncall): ops note — we can rotate on behalf for managed components; for customer-managed IAM principals we can only recommend. For cust-phi-1 they use our managed connector so we rotated their connector creds and recorded rotation event: `rotation_id=rot-20260315-01`. For cust-pii-2 it's customer-managed, flagged in support ticket.

Mona (Legal): good. Draft notice should differentiate managed vs unmanaged and avoid definitive claims about data access. Also include timeline, what we know, next steps, and contact for dedicated support.

Alex R (SRE): internal status page draft for ops channel (short):

"Status: Degraded — Potential credential exposure in Private deployments sync logs. Impact: possible exposure of short-lived credentials for 2 customers. Mitigation: rotated managed connector creds for one customer, patch deployed to remove env dumps, investigating cloudtrail for misuse. ETA for initial update: 60 minutes"

Ben (oncall): can someone post that to status-internal and start a public status page entry (initial) with redaction? We should avoid naming customers on public page.

Jia (Ops): posting internal now. Will open public initial status (maintenance) entry: `We are investigating reports of potential credential exposure in Private deployments. Affected customers are being contacted directly. We will provide updates as our investigation proceeds.` Going live in 10m.

Priya S: security checklist we've run:
- rotate any rotated/managed creds (done for cust-phi-1)
- kill any lingering tokens/sessions
- revoke ingestion queue access keys
- patch helper image to drop env dumps (deployed)
- run CloudTrail & token-use correlation (in progress)

Ben (oncall): Priya taking lead after handoff. Priya, please keep Legal looped and prepare a short (1-2 paragraph) customer notice for each customer that specifies whether we rotated creds on their behalf or not. Mona to approve.

Mona (Legal): I'll review drafts in 20m. If any PHI is at risk and we confirm access, we need to follow mandatory notification timelines. For now treat as potential exposure.

Tyler (CS): I've created support tickets: #INC-8492 (cust-phi-1) and #INC-8493 (cust-pii-2). Adding customers and account contacts. Holding outreach until Legal signoff.

IncidentBot: Reminder: Next handover in 30m. Escalation policy engaged: if scope increases to >5 customers or confirmed misuse, escalate to Execs.

Priya S: drafting customer notices now. Posting drafts here for review: 

--- DRAFT (cust-phi-1, managed connector) ---
Hi <CustomerContact>,
We detected short-lived credentials for your connector in temporary logs on 2026-03-15. We have rotated the connector credentials on your behalf and deployed a fix to prevent similar logging in the future. We have not found evidence that the credentials were used to access your resources. Recommended actions for you: review your access logs and reach out if you see anything unexpected. We will send a follow-up report with details within 72 hours.

--- DRAFT (cust-pii-2, customer-managed) ---
Hi <CustomerContact>,
We detected short-lived credentials associated with your sync task in temporary logs on 2026-03-15. These credentials appear to be customer-managed; we have not rotated them. We recommend you rotate the impacted credentials immediately and review access logs in your cloud account. Our team is available to assist. We have no evidence of credential misuse at this time.

Priya S: Please review and sign off or propose edits.

Mona (Legal): edits: add contact for security questions and a line about what we will include in the follow-up report (timeline, root cause, mitigations, scope). Also remove the phrase "we have not found evidence" -> replace with "as of [time], we have not observed evidence of unauthorized use".

Ben (oncall): sounds good. Once Mona approves, Tyler please queue ticket for customer outreach and include legal-approved copy. Jia, keep patch pinned until we confirm no regression.

Alex R (SRE): continuing cloudtrail correlation. Current status: no third-party API calls with those keys through 1710409000. Will update if anything changes.

Jia (Ops): patch stable, image version `private-sync:2026.03.15` promoted to stable.

Tyler (CS): queued outreach drafts pending legal signoff.

Mona (Legal): I approve the updated wording with the minor edits. Priya, please paste final copies here and I'll provide a one-line legal approval for each.

Priya S: final drafts posted above with Mona edits applied.

Mona (Legal): Approved for cust-phi-1 (managed). Approved for cust-pii-2 (customer-managed) with the note that we must include support ticket links and the follow-up timeline.

Ben (oncall): handing off to Priya as of 1710408200. Priya, you own outreach and the 72h report. I'll stay in thread as backup.

Priya S: acknowledged. I'll send the customer messages through the support ticket right now and start the 72-hour postmortem template.

IncidentBot: RESOLUTION UPDATE: initial containment complete. Next update (72-hour report) scheduled. Close thread when postmortem published.

Ben (oncall): great work team.

Priya S: will post final incident report link here when ready.
